title: Investigating Triggers and Strategies for Reducing Online Racism in Sport Events: A Discourse Analysis
content: Racism remains a pervasive issue in sports, significantly impacting individuals, communities, and the integrity of the sporting environment. The advent of online platforms has exacerbated this issue, enabling the proliferation of racial discrimination through digital hate speech that transcends physical and cultural boundaries. This study examines the antecedents and mitigation strategies for online racism in sports events, employing a discourse analysis approach. Utilizing qualitative data sourced from platforms such as Reddit, Quora, blogs, and online news forums, the findings reveal key drivers of online racism, including anonymity, lack of accountability, perceptions of digital freedom of expression, and tribalism among sports fans. These factors create environments conducive to the expression and normalization of racist behaviors. To counteract this phenomenon, the study identifies effective interventions, including legislative frameworks, Al-driven content moderation systems, and robust reporting mechanisms. This research contributes to the academic discourse on digital racism by highlighting the structural and behavioral dynamics underlying its manifestation in sports contexts. The study also offers practical implications for policymakers, platform managers, and sports organizations seeking to combat digital hate speech and foster more inclusive online communities.
